state_reason: statement.week.change is the one mutating endpoint: the new statementWeek/statementDay must persist for that card so later statement.week.get / cards.balance / statement.week.decide calls see it (decide itself is preview-only), and the 401-once token path also spans calls.

identity.notes: This contract defines no identity verification: customerNo alone identifies the customer, no endpoint asks a question or counts wrong answers, and no tool is gated behind a verification step, so the mock must not invent verify_identity or an identity-not-verified refusal here. The only credential in the contract is the transport bearer token, checked by exactly one endpoint (statement.week.change -> 401 when missing or expired).

fields: calls[] {seq, at, customer_id, tool, request, result} — every tool call in order; customer_id is this contract's customerNo; tool is the operationId (cards_list, cards_balance, statement_week_get, statement_week_decide, statement_week_change, contact_email_get, statement_pdf_send); request/result hold the JSON bodies as sent and returned plus the HTTP status, so injected 400/401/404/500 and delays are visible
outcome — overall run outcome derived from the contract's own vocabulary (see extra_notes); null while undetermined
reason — short machine-readable reason for the outcome
promises[] {product_id, amount, date} — structure only; this contract has no promise endpoint, keep []
identity {verified, wrong_answers, locked} — structure only; this contract has no identity step, keep {verified: null, wrong_answers: 0, locked: false}

statementWeekChanges[] {customer_id, cardNumber, from {statementWeek, statementDay}, to {statementWeek, statementDay}, decide {statementDate, statementDueDate, statementDay}, change {responseCode, responseMessage, exitState}} — the cross-call state a scorer will check

read_routes.summary: the ledger a scorer reads for one customer (customer_id = customerNo): every tool call in order with its request and result
all customers' ledgers, for whole-run scoring

response.variables: call variables incl. a fresh customer_id — for this contract a customerNo, plus the cards/statement/contact fixtures the mock will serve for it

sessions.notes: The contract defines no session/bootstrap endpoint and no token endpoint: every tool is called directly with customerNo/cardNumber and the 401 on statement.week.change is handled out of band. Propose this practice-style route so a hidden case can be started and handed a fresh customer_id (customerNo) that the mock serves deterministically.

faults.tool: any service whose customer fixture carries delaySeconds
faults.when: whenever the fixture for that service/card/week defines delaySeconds
faults.behavior: wait that many seconds before answering, then return the recorded 200 response normally (delay, not error)

faults.when: when injected by the case (the contract lists this 500 on every path)
faults.behavior: 500 FBE00099 — Technical error on Freya's side

faults.when: token missing or expired (the contract's only 401)
faults.behavior: 401 once; the caller gets a new token and retries once, and the retried call must succeed

products.shape: card (one product unit here): {cardNumber: string, masked in the test env as first 6 + last 4 e.g. "540000******1234"; cardNumberLast4: string; productName: string (free text, e.g. "Yıldız Pratik Classic" / "Yıldız Tasarım"); status: "A"; isMainCard: boolean}; its balance adds statementDate/lastPayDate/nextStatementDate/nextLastPayDate (dd.MM.yyyy), per-currency debt blocks debtTL/debtUSD/debtEUR/debtGBP each {statementPaymentStatus: "HAS_DEBT"|"NO_DEBT", transferAmount: number, statementDebt: number, minPayment: number, remainingDebt: number, remainingMinPayment: number, currentPeriodExpense: number, totalDebt: number, totalDebtPaymentStatus: "HAS_DEBT"|"NO_DEBT", remainAutomaticPaymentAmount: number} (amounts are numbers with 2 decimals, e.g. 5000.13), top-level statementPaymentStatus/totalDebtPaymentStatus and automaticPaymentFlag: "Y"|"N"
products.ids: No separate product id exists in this contract: a product is addressed by the masked cardNumber exactly as cards.list returned it (test BINs 540000/545000 + six stars + last 4). Key fixtures on that exact string — cards.balance answers with a DIFFERENT mask of the same card (first 4 + last 4, "5400********1234") and cardNumberLast4 is not unique across a customer's cards, so never match or rebuild ids from the digits.

unknown_customer_policy: Contract first: seed customers are replayed verbatim. The contract's only not-found outcomes are 404 FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102 (customer has no valid card) on cards.list, 404 FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120 on cards.balance and 404 FB_IVR_CHANNEL_121 on statement.week.get (card not found), and 404 FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107 (no statement document to send) on statement.pdf.send. For a customerNo or cardNumber that is not in the seed, do NOT 500 and do not blanket-404: derive a deterministic fixture from the id (stable hash; the same id must get the same answers across calls and restarts) — 1-3 active cards with cards.list-style masks, a statement week/day and the 5/9/16/23-day date cycle, HAS_DEBT/NO_DEBT debt blocks per currency, an ibanEmail, and week 2/3/4 charted for statement.week.decide — so hidden customers behave exactly like seeded ones.
extra_notes: Response envelope (from the fixtures, not shown in the OpenAPI): every 200 body in TEST CUSTOMERS is wrapped as {data: <the schema the contract documents>, result: {guid: 32-hex, returnCode: "1", messageText: "Success", code: "1", message: "Success", type: null, details: {guid: <same>, rootCause: null, errorOrigin: null}}}. Serve that envelope (a fresh guid per call, identical in result.guid and result.details.guid) and read the contract's documented fields from inside data.

Error bodies: the contract names only the code strings (INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR, FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102, FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107, FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120, FB_IVR_CHANNEL_121, FBE00099) with their statuses; it defines no error body shape, so keep the same data/result envelope and carry the code in result.code/result.message — do not invent new field names.

No outcome/reason vocabulary is defined by this contract: success is per service (result.returnCode "1" with message "Success", exitState "1_CARD"/"MULTI_CARD"/"OK"/"DONE", responseCode 0 with responseMessage "00" or "Success"). Derive the ledger's outcome/reason from those values or leave them null — do not import promise/callback/transfer vocabulary this contract does not have.

The TEST CUSTOMERS excerpt supplied here is truncated (it ends mid-file inside statement.week.decide for the second customer): further customers and customer 92030487's statement.week.change, contact.email.get and statement.pdf.send fixtures were not readable. Re-extract the full file before freezing fixtures, and check the truncated part for any first-call failure injection — the visible text documents delaySeconds as the only injection knob.

Contract semantics the mock must honour: only status "A" cards are listed; cards.balance accepts the cards.list mask verbatim and replies with a different mask; statement.week.decide mutates nothing while statement.week.change does and the change must persist per card; deciding the week the card already has is an error; statement.week.change returns statementWeek and statementDay as strings; contact.email.get answers identically for E, P and B and 400s only on an empty type; statement.pdf.send sends to the emailAddress it is given without checking registration; only statement.week.change can 401 and the retry is once with a new token.

Derived date model from the fixtures (use it for hidden customers): statement days are week 1 -> 5, week 2 -> 9, week 3 -> 16, week 4 -> 23; statement.week.decide returns the first such date in the cycle AFTER the current statement (fixture: current 05.10.2026 / next 05.11.2026 -> week 2 = 09.11.2026, week 3 = 16.11.2026, week 4 = 23.11.2026) and the due date is the statement date + 10 days (19.11.2026 / 26.11.2026 / 03.12.2026), returned in statementDueDate. Week 1 is the card's current week.

Test customers seen: 90000001 (Ada Örnek, one card, Yıldız Pratik Classic, exitState 1_CARD) and 92030487 (Ilgaz Güler, four cards — 540000******4253, 545000******4253, 540000******6184, 540000******8870 — exitState MULTI_CARD, including two cards sharing last4 4253). Turkish retail customers with Turkish product names and TL debt, hence language "tr"; transport and JSON field names and messages stay English.

Joint statements: statement.week.get can return relationType "M"/"C" together with relatedCardNumber and relatedCardProductName pointing at the paired card (both seen customers return ""). Support a hidden pair whose two cards reference each other, and keep relationType empty string for ordinary cards.

Scope: this contract covers only the card/statement/contact voice tool API. It contains no debt-collection, identity, promise, callback or transfer endpoint — anything of that kind belongs to a separate contract and must not be synthesized into this mock.

Server and tool names: the contract's server is https://api.freyabank.example with path prefix /voice/v1; the operationIds are the tool names (cards_list, cards_balance, statement_week_get, statement_week_decide, statement_week_change, contact_email_get, statement_pdf_send). aiFlow is required on cards.list but not validated; customerNo is accepted as string or number and cardNumber must be echoed unchanged.
